title: A Garden for the Letters
premise: Hazel Voss built a career planning other people's perfect days while keeping her own heart locked down, sustained for ten years by anonymous letters exchanged through a PO box with someone who signed only 'Wren.' When Wren—actually baker Theo Lindqvist, who has just leased the shop next door to Hazel's wedding-planning studio—moves into the neighborhood, the letters' author and recipient collide without either knowing it at first. As a failing bakery lease, a career-defining celebrity wedding, and Hazel's fear of being truly seen converge, they discover each other's identities at the worst possible moment. Hazel must choose between the controlled life that once saved her and the vulnerable love she's been rehearsing in ink for a decade—and she chooses love, signing her final letter with her real name as the bakery's lease is renewed by a community that refuses to let them go.
about_author: Freya Eriksen is a former stationery-shop owner from coastal Maine who still writes letters by hand every Sunday. She believes the best love stories are the ones people almost talk themselves out of.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She runs a flawless wedding for clients who cry happy tears while she feels nothing, then returns to her empty studio and rereads a decade of letters from 'Wren,' her only intimacy. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control; establishes her belief that hearts are trainable.

chapters.title: Flour Next Door
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He signs the lease on the bakery beside Hazel's studio, unpacking boxes that include a shoebox of letters he's never sent—the ones he wrote back but kept. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by cowardice; he recognizes his new neighbor's name and freezes.

chapters.title: Terms of Neutrality
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First meeting: Hazel offers Theo a strictly professional welcome basket and rules about shared walls and noise. Banter sparks something neither names. Beat: attraction denied at the door; Hazel schedules him like a vendor.

chapters.title: Cardamom at Closing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Late-night baking mishap floods the shared hallway; Hazel helps salvage trays, and they talk until 2 a.m. over cardamom buns. Beat: first crack in her armor; she goes home and writes Wren a letter admitting she met someone.

chapters.title: The Marlowe Wedding
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A career-making celebrity client hires her, demanding perfection on an impossible timeline. Her assistant Priya pushes back against Hazel's joyless efficiency. Beat: rising stakes; duty tightening its grip just as feeling becomes possible.

chapters.title: What Wren Never Sent
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His sister Marta finds the unsent letters and confronts him: ten years of loving someone in secret isn't romance, it's hiding. Beat: guilt and longing; he drafts a confession and burns it, unable to risk losing the letters entirely.

chapters.title: Tasting Menu
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo caters a tasting for Hazel's Marlowe wedding; their professional collaboration turns electric over a shared counter. Beat: falling in motion—they build something together and pretend it's business.

chapters.title: Lease Clauses
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The landlord raises the bakery rent beyond survival; Theo hides the crisis, ashamed. Meanwhile Hazel notices his exhaustion and misreads it as waning interest. Beat: miscommunication compounds; both retreat behind their walls.

chapters.title: Rain on the Awning
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Trapped under one awning in a storm, Hazel nearly tells Theo about the letters; he nearly tells her he's Wren. Both swerve. Beat: the almost-confession; yearning at its most unbearable.

chapters.title: Priya Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Priya calls out her boss: 'You plan love for strangers and starve yourself of it.' Found-family beat: Priya and Marta meet and conspire, comparing notes neither knows matches. Beat: warmth and comic relief before the fall.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marlowe rehearsal dinner succeeds spectacularly; Hazel and Theo celebrate afterward, and the night ends in a kiss. Beat: peak happiness—the calm the story will break against.

chapters.title: Morning After, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Terrified by how right it felt, Hazel reverts to control: she reframes the kiss as a lapse, proposes 'boundaries.' Beat: self-sabotage; the muscle theory reasserted, cruelly.

chapters.title: Marta's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Marta gives him a deadline: tell Hazel or lose her respect too. The landlord serves formal notice—thirty days. Beat: pressure from all sides; Theo decides to confess everything, in person, tonight.

chapters.title: Wrong Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo arrives at Hazel's studio with the letters in hand just as she leaves for the venue; they miss each other by minutes, twice. Beat: dramatic irony tightened to snapping point.

chapters.title: The Letter on the Counter
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Theo leaves the shoebox with Priya; Hazel opens it and reads her own decade reflected back—every letter she sent, answered in handwriting she now recognizes from bakery receipts. Beat: revelation; devastation and wonder at once.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Cold Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hazel finds Theo mid-bake and demands why he hid. He says he was afraid of being nothing without the letters; she says she built a whole person out of them. Brutal, honest fight. Beat: climax of emotional conflict—love exposed as mutual fear.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The eviction notice posts publicly; Hazel, wounded, throws herself into the Marlowe wedding and accepts a partnership offer in another city. Beat: darkest hour—both choose duty, and it fits badly.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the flawless Marlowe ceremony, watching genuine vows, Hazel realizes she's been officiating her own avoidance for years. She walks out mid-reception, leaving Priya in charge. Beat: turning point; identity reclaimed over career.

chapters.title: Last Letter, First Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hazel writes Wren one final letter—signed Hazel Voss—and slips it under the bakery door along with a plan: neighbors, customers, and Priya have quietly organized to buy the building's lease together. Beat: vulnerability as action; found family made literal.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He reads the letter as the community gathers outside; he answers not in ink but at the door, saying her name aloud for the first time. Kiss in flour-dusted daylight. Beat: resolution of the central romance; invisibility ended.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Letters
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Epilogue-adjacent: they convert the alley between studio and bakery into a garden where the letters are buried like seeds—not destroyed, just finally allowed to grow into something living. Beat: integration of past and present.

chapters.title: Sunday, By Hand
chapters.summary: Dual POV coda. Months later: Hazel plans weddings again, but differently—with Priya as partner; Theo's bakery thrives. They still write Sunday letters, delivered by hand, three steps apart. Final line echoes chapter one: the heart is a muscle after all—it grows. Beat: quiet, earned joy.
